newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Some European ADRs firm in New York.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Some European ADRs firm in New York.

text.p: Shares of some European companies traded in the United States were strong on company-specific news while shares of Telefonica del Peru SA, the main Peruvian ADR, recovered slightly.
Among the European companies making a good showing in New York was Spanish banking group Banco Santander SA, which was up 1-7/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Santander said it had been awarded a majority stake in Banco Venezuela.
French oil company Elf Aquitaine announced that its Sanofi pharmaceuticals subsidiary would be free to seek a merger with other drug laboratories.
Financial analysts said that Britain's Zeneca Group Plc and Warner-Lambert Co of the United States were the best placed for a possible aaliance with Sanofi.
Elf shares were up 3-1/2 at 45-3/8 on the NYSE.
Peru's Telefonica del Peru SA was up 3/4 at 18-1/4 after a sharp sell-off yesterday on concern about the hostage crisis at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima.
The stock sold off to 18 from 19-1/4 on volume of three million shares on Wednesday. Analysts said that the volume was very high for the stock.
"Three million shares is a big deal for the stock," said Peter Greenbaum, who follows Peru at Smith Barney.
The brokerage earlier today reduced its weighting for Peru in its Latin American portfolio to neutral from overweight.
"(Our) view is that as this goes on the (Peruvian) market will go down. We don't see a high probability of a quick and successful solution," Greenbaum said.
